verdict.rationale: Obsidian's own design keeps vaults as local plain-text Markdown files on your device. Users can open any folder as a vault, which gives them direct control over where their data physically resides, and a community user corroborates that notes stay only on their machine and chosen sync service. However, the first-party cloud services (Obsidian Sync and Publish) have no documented region or residency selection. Third-party sync providers are user-side arrangements and earn no credit. Missing for 10: region/residency choice for Obsidian Sync and Publish servers, documentation of where Obsidian-hosted data is located.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device. You have total control over your data
You can open multiple folders as individual vaults, for example to separate notes for work and school.
Notes are stored only on their machine and sync service
